design: v7 — one universal SQLite table; every crawler upserts into it via crawl_store.store(). Source-agnostic CONTRACT: crawlers bend their data into this shape, the shape never bends per site. Weight + packaging dimensions are REAL writable columns (not JSON, not generated) so they sort/filter/UPDATE freely and survive back-fill; only volumetric/chargeable weight are generated from them. Identity is a single generated dedup_key (source + external_id, else source + url). Real DDL: schema.sql (source of truth). Ingest: crawl_store.py.
target: SQLite (generated STORED columns + json_extract). Migrate to Postgres later with the same shape if scale demands.

canonical_units.note: Every crawler MUST convert into these before ingest — the point of a shared contract is that a column means the same thing across all sources.
canonical_units.price: numeric value in commercial.price.value with an explicit commercial.price.currency (ISO like VND, USD). Never mix currencies in one column without the currency tag.

identity_rule: Every row must be addressable by external_id OR url (CHECK ck_identity). url may be NULL for API sources with no per-product page — do NOT invent synthetic URLs; rely on external_id. dedup_key = source + '|' + coalesce(external_id, url).
price_history: Sibling append-only table `price_history` (see schema.sql). `product` holds the latest snapshot; price_history keeps EVERY distinct price observed over time (time-based discounts included) — never overwritten, never picked. crawl_store.store() appends a row whenever the price differs from the last observation for that dedup_key. Columns: dedup_key, source, external_id, price_value, currency, stock_status, account_tier, observed_at. Same product crawled under different sources/tiers (dealer vs public retail) accumulates independent price series — join product rows by external_id for dealer-vs-retail margin.

written_columns.note: Written directly by crawl_store.store(). Weight/packaging dims are plain writable columns so they can be back-filled with a normal UPDATE (coalesce on upsert protects a manual back-fill from being wiped by a later re-crawl).

product_shape.brand: string, nullable — single field, raw/normalized split dropped until a normalize pipeline exists
product_shape.category: string, nullable — NOT every source exposes a category; leave NULL rather than fake one

specification_shape.note: Product technical dims/weight (as a spec) live here as items (e.g. items.Weight). This is DIFFERENT from packaging: spec = the product's own physical attributes; the pack_* / *_weight_kg columns = the shipping carton.

price.currency: string, nullable — ISO code, REQUIRED whenever value is set

commercial_shape.unit: string, nullable — selling unit (pcs, m, kg...)
commercial_shape.pricing_limitation: ONE price per row = the price the crawling account sees. Tier/account is recorded in crawl.account_tier. Multi-tier / qty-break pricing is NOT modeled — to capture multiple tiers, crawl once per account (they land as separate rows only if source differs, else last write wins). Extend with a price_tiers array later if a real need appears.

crawl_shape.status: string, required — enum: success, partial, failed
crawl_shape.score: number, required — parse-confidence 0..100; set 100 for structured APIs where parsing can't fail
crawl_shape.account_tier: string, nullable — which account/tier the price/stock reflects (e.g. dealer login email)

null_strategy.enums_with_unknown_state: stock.status and crawl.status always populated, default "unknown", never NULL.

constraints: UNIQUE(dedup_key) — the single upsert target (source + external_id, else source + url)
CHECK ck_identity — external_id IS NOT NULL OR url IS NOT NULL
product_name indexed BTREE for prefix search; add an FTS5 mirror table if full-text ranking is needed
changes_this_round: v7: synced this doc to the real schema.sql — prior v6 doc described a `packaging` JSON column and JSON-sourced weight columns that the implementation does NOT have
Weight + packaging dims documented as REAL writable columns (net/gross_weight_kg, pack_L/W/H_cm); only volumetric/chargeable are generated from them
Added canonical_units block (kg / cm / currency-tagged price) — mandatory conversion contract so a column means the same across every source
product.category relaxed to nullable (not every source has one) — matches reality, no faking
url relaxed to nullable + identity_rule (external_id OR url) enforced by CHECK ck_identity — no synthetic URL pollution for API sources
id fixed to INTEGER (was ambiguous BIGINT|UUID)
raw_hash note corrected: raw payload (HTML or JSON), not 'raw HTML' only
Documented the single-price limitation explicitly (one price per row = crawling account's price; tier in crawl.account_tier)
PhuThaiTech remains first producer: API gives no weight/dims -> those columns NULL, back-fillable later
